question.text: Let the focus<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mi>S</mi><mo>)</mo></math> of a parabola divides its one of the focal chords <math><mi>P</mi><mi>Q</mi></math> in the ratio <math><mn>2</mn><mo>:</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo></math> If the tangent at <math><mi>Q</mi></math> cuts the directrix at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> such that <math><mi>R</mi><mi>Q</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo></math> then the distance (in units) of the focus from the tangent at <math><mi>P</mi></math> is

solution.text:
Let, the foot of the perpendicular from the focus on the tangent PR is A which lies on the tangent at the vertex.
Also, ∠PRQ=90o
Now, in ΔPRQ & ΔPAS,∠P is common & ∠R=∠A
Then, ΔPRQ is similar to ΔPAS
⇒PSPQ=ASRQ=23⇒AS=23×6=4
⇒ The distance of the focus from the tangent at P=4 units
